## Reading and refinement

Read the entire founder specification, the complete NSM v20 chart, the workflow's complete operating sections, and the notebook's methods and latest results. Read all 296 distinct native time-period glosses and all 106 native people-group glosses in `022-native-scope-inventory.json`. The location inventory is ranging only; its 1,349 native sense groups have not received a complete source review or a warrant.

The parent screens find 396 open WHEN targets and 148 open PEOPLE targets, with no opposing stored singleton. Unknown targets supply no confirmation. Reviewing complete definitions exposes scope challenges before admission. The child conditions describe the defining head rather than adding individual word exceptions.

The existing `native_noun_frames` vocabulary now includes `temporal_extent` and `human_collective`. The former requires a declared temporal extent head with explicit *time*, including *time period/interval/span*. The latter requires a literal people head or a group/class/body/collection of people/persons/human beings. Possessives, unrelated heads, alternative genera, coordinated extensions and multiple glosses remain outside these deliberately narrow constructions. Existing frame membership is unchanged. Source applicability still requires the existing exact WordNet or Wiktionary native witness. A matching sentence, association, spelling, derived-form candidate or missing source packet cannot activate a rule.

Read every complete gloss in the resulting child inventory: 47 native sense groups for temporal extent and 54 for human collectivity. The scope census records 59 temporal definitions (30 Wiktionary, 29 WordNet), with 47 open targets and 12 existing positives; and 71 collective definitions (12 Wiktionary, 59 WordNet), all targets open. These are census results, not admitted fills. No observed child gloss contradicts its stated defining genus. The twelve temporal positives retain their pre-existing proof roots and are not twelve independent laws.

## Temporal extent warrant

The approved catalogue maps NSM TIME~WHEN to GSE WHEN. The chart explicitly distinguishes times, moments, and intervals of unspecified/short/long extent. A definition headed by an explicit period or interval of time therefore has its own temporal content. The source's exact qualifier may describe sleeping, employment, an orbit, fishing, a legal term, or childbirth without changing that temporal head. This supplies WHEN alone. It supplies neither a fixed duration, QUANTITY, LONG_TIME, BODY, BE, nor an event's participant roles. Those remain separately justified questions.

The rule does not identify the interval's location in a sentence's timeline. Existing sentence geometry owns attachment, temporal links and grammatical binding. The special `(FOR) SOME TIME` catalogue construction remains sentence-level and excluded from lexical assignments.

## Human collective warrant

The saved chart's PEOPLE unit denotes people collectively and permits quantification over these people. The existing primitive registry calls PEOPLE a collective substantive. A complete native noun definition headed by people or an explicitly human collection supplies this content directly. A lexicalized collective sense of *room* is distinct from its spatial sense. A plural group of dead people does not thereby become alive: PEOPLE supplies no ALIVE, BODY, first/second-person reference or desire assignment. A definition describing one person or an object used by people does not establish this collective head.

## Audit and execution contract

The frozen plan uses two Zipf-prioritized teaching steps and three held-out questions per family, including exact senses from both dictionary sources. Held-out lemmas and native sense groups remain disjoint from teaching. Each request withholds the proposed rule, its conclusion and descendants. The target stays open under the prior baseline. The typed writer supplies only the requested missing bank or null, with full native context and the current other-bank constraints.

The controller now permits a witnessed unary WordNet ancestry family without inventing an unrelated bank premise. The reviewed exporter and resolver already supported this form. A real-entry-point test reproduces teaching, disjoint auditing, rule admission, migration and replay; missing ancestry, missing native-lemma witnesses and invalid guards are refused. The production children above use the existing cross-source native-frame path.

Publication requires the exact staged full-cohort delta, complete replay, retained unknown and explicit-zero states, cumulative semantic controls, ordinary encoder compilation, sentence/ambiguity/state benchmarks and the existing sparse runtime gate. Preserve the active release, one rollback, original sources and all unique audit records. Count teaching, audits, retries and adjudications separately. A disagreement remains evidence to interpret; it is not automatically a semantic counterexample or a zero to commit.

# Nondeictic physical naming: specification-learning round

This is a new measured phase under `gse.ssl-construction/2`, following the
singleton-only controller diagnosis. Its records belong beside the existing
lexicon experiment records; it is not a second construction design.

The founder's approved boundary is first-/second-person reference only;
generic selfhood does not supply I or YOU. The exact decision is retained in
`023-approved-person-reference-boundary.json`. The native closed-class I/YOU
definitions are positive controls. The approved generic self definition is an
outside-scope negative control, not an empirical audit result.

The candidate mechanism is own-word naming versus discourse deixis. An exact
native noun definition naming a physical non-person entity or kind does not
thereby refer to the current speaker or addressee. Under the approved bank
meanings its own content is orthogonal to I and YOU. Sentence-level reference
binding and any participant described in its gloss remain separate. This is a
positive type/role argument, not a zero supplied by a missing source field.

The initial sufficient scope is the conjunction of noun POS, an attested native
lemma, a witnessed WordNet `physical_entity.n.01` ancestry and witnessed exclusion
from `person.n.01` ancestry. Both ancestry predicates must be established from
the same exact definition's stored native paths. This deliberately reserves
person/address/pronominal definitions. It does not claim that physicality is a
necessary condition for nondeictic naming, or that every noun has zero deixis.
World associations, alias spellings and unrelated senses cannot activate it.

The first Zipf-aware teaching frontier consists of the exact ordinary water,
body and rock senses. Their source definitions must be inspected and their
eligibility established before frequency orders them. Aggregate spelling
frequency is labelled as such; it is not attributed to a rare homograph.
Holdouts span animals, plants, artifacts and matter, use distinct native senses
and spellings, and are disjoint from teaching. The proposed rules and their
answers are withheld from direct audit requests.

Stage each rule separately and together over the entire eligible population.
Retain exact contradictions, model-prefix reconsiderations, partial narrowing
and joint-space contraction. Independent model disagreement is a typed challenge
to inspect, not grounds for inventing an exception or voting a sign into place.
Admission requires the semantic warrant and successful independent audits;
model agreement alone is not semantic gold. If a counterexample changes the
guard, record the narrower mechanism and re-stage the entire scope.

Measure baseline, direct teaching and rule propagation separately, including
the full-lexicon frequency buckets. An accepted model prefix may be archived by
the existing rule migration when its context changes; reopened cells remain
unknown and are reported. Full replay is required before publication. This
round does not claim to complete the lexicon, all foundational laws, general
rule-universe discovery, or the common-language runtime checkpoint.
